rules: OGL use of INSPIRE Index Polygons is free of charge.
Failure to comply with OGL conditions automatically ends the rights granted under the licence.
Reuse under the OGL requires acknowledgement of HM Land Registry as the data source.
Reuse of INSPIRE polygon geometry requires the current Ordnance Survey attribution using AC0000851063.
Where possible, reusers must provide a link to HM Land Registry's INSPIRE conditions of use.
INSPIRE Index Polygons are an open source dataset developed for the INSPIRE Directive.
The INSPIRE dataset contains locations of freehold registered property in England and Wales.
INSPIRE is a subset of HM Land Registry's Index Polygons database for freehold land and property.
A polygon on a local-authority boundary can appear in both local-authority data files.
Each INSPIRE Index Polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID related to a registered title.
A registered title has one title number but can contain several separate polygons.
Each separate polygon belonging to a title has its own Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
Absence of a Land Registry-INSPIRE ID can indicate that land is not registered.
Absence of a Land Registry-INSPIRE ID can instead indicate a leasehold registration.
Other tenure types not present in INSPIRE can also explain absence of an INSPIRE ID.
The extent of land in a registered title cannot be established from INSPIRE polygons alone.
The individual title plan is required to identify the registered title's extent.
HM Land Registry's Find a Property service can use an INSPIRE ID to obtain title registration and plan information.
GML is an open data format widely used across Europe.
HM Land Registry states that GML complies with the EU INSPIRE Directive.
HM Land Registry uses GML to provide a standard data structure for GIS and CAD systems.
GML may need conversion to another GIS format for use in a target system.
When GML is converted for another tool, the data must also use an appropriate projection.
HM Land Registry gives conversion from GML to KML as an example for use in Google Maps.
QGIS is identified by HM Land Registry as a free open-source system for viewing and converting GML.
In National Polygon technical data, Shape is a mandatory Geometry field and the index-polygon geometry must be a single area.
In National Polygon technical data, Poly_ID is a mandatory numeric field and is the unique polygon reference.
In National Polygon technical data, Title_No is a mandatory character field identifying a registered title.
In National Polygon technical data, INSERT is a mandatory date recording initial polygon creation on the index map.
In National Polygon technical data, UPDATE is a mandatory date recording when all or part of the title was last updated.
In National Polygon technical data, Vers_No is a mandatory numeric field representing the version of Poly_ID.
In National Polygon technical data, Rec_Status is mandatory and uses A, C and D for added, changed and deleted.
The Planning Data API exposes more than 100 planning and housing datasets for England through one interface.
Planning Data states that its API is still in beta and may change for production systems.
The entity API period parameter controls whether current entries or all entries are included.
The entity API start_date_year parameter is an integer used with start_date_match.
The entity API start_date_month parameter is an integer used with start_date_match.
The entity API start_date_day parameter is an integer used with start_date_match.
The entity API start_date_match accepts match, before, since or an empty value.
The entity API end_date_year parameter is an integer used with end_date_match.
The entity API end_date_month parameter is an integer used with end_date_match.
The entity API end_date_day parameter is an integer used with end_date_match.
The entity API end_date_match accepts match, before, since or an empty value.
The entity API entry_date_year parameter is an integer used with entry_date_match.
The entity API entry_date_month parameter is an integer used with entry_date_match.
The entity API entry_date_day parameter is an integer used with entry_date_match.
The entity API entry_date_match accepts match, before, since or an empty value.
Planning Data documentation warns that absence of API results does not prove that no planning constraints exist because coverage varies by area.
Planning Data documents a single request capable of returning all 337 local planning authorities by using dataset=local-planning-authority and limit=500.
Listed-building entities can include listed_building_grade directly without a separate lookup.
The planning-application data specification is documented as still in development.
Local planning authorities are not currently required to share planning-application data to that developing specification.
The Environment Agency Time Stamped DTM product is an archive of raster elevation data produced from site-specific LIDAR surveys.
Environment Agency site-specific LIDAR surveys have been carried out across England since 1998.
Some areas, including coastal zones, have been surveyed multiple times in the Time Stamped archive.
Time Stamped DTM data is available at varying resolutions of 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m depending on project requirements.
The Time Stamped DTM is produced from the last-return LIDAR signal.
Environment Agency removes surface objects from the DSM using bespoke algorithms and manual editing to create the Time Stamped DTM.
Time Stamped DTM rasters are downloadable as GeoTIFF data in 5km zip files.
Time Stamped DTM elevation values are presented in metres.
Time Stamped DTM elevations are referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
Time Stamped DTM data is aligned to the OS National Grid.
Environment Agency states vertical accuracy of +/-15cm RMSE for its LIDAR data.
The transformation used on Time Stamped DTM data is specific to the survey time period.
The Time Stamped metadata index can identify which data is available at a location.
The Time Stamped metadata index records specific survey dates.
The Time Stamped metadata index records product resolution.
The Time Stamped metadata index records the transformation and geoidal model used.
The current 1m LIDAR Composite metadata identifier is 13787b9a-26a4-4775-8523-806d13af58fc.
The 1m LIDAR Composite metadata gives a creation date of 8 February 2023.
The 1m LIDAR Composite metadata gives a revision date of 15 December 2023.
The 1m LIDAR Composite metadata gives a geographic latitude extent from 49.943 to 55.816.
The 1m LIDAR Composite metadata gives a geographic longitude extent from -6.236 to 2.072.
The 1m LIDAR Composite metadata exposes a WMS service.
The 1m LIDAR Composite metadata exposes a WCS service.
The 1m LIDAR Composite metadata exposes a WMTS service.
The 1m LIDAR Composite metadata exposes an OGC API Features service.
Environment Agency changed LiDAR Composite and SurfZone survey metadata indexes so download ZIPs contain GeoPackage rather than Shapefile index data.
The GeoPackage survey metadata index describes the spatial location of raster elevation data.
The GeoPackage survey metadata index describes the temporal extent of raster elevation data.
For a 1m DSM, Environment Agency documents an average point-cloud density of at least 1 point per square metre across the survey.
Environment Agency cautions that DTM point density under vegetation need not reach 1 point per square metre even for a 1m product.
The source DTM for OS Terrain products is captured as a triangulated irregular network using mass points, breaklines and/or automated photogrammetric techniques.
Ordnance Survey states that a TIN can retain feature edges more accurately than a grid because it models the surface with triangles.
Both OS Terrain 50 grid and contour products are interpolated from the source TIN model.
OS Terrain 50 generalises feature modelling because it is designed to work with small-scale products.
OS Terrain 50 minimum coverage extends to the low-water mark defined using Hydrographic Office information.
For England and Wales the low-water coverage reference is Mean Low Water.
For Scotland the low-water coverage reference is Mean Low Water Springs.
Land wholly within inland water bodies that is represented as topographic-area features is captured according to positional-accuracy requirements.
The minimum capture requirement for such land in inland water bodies is the outer edge of the feature.
Surrounding inland water is modelled as flat.
Other land within inland water bodies captured by automated processes is removed from the terrain data.
Source TIN z-values are subject to positional-accuracy requirements that vary by geographic classification.
The three source-terrain classifications are urban and major communication routes, rural, and mountain and moorland.
Bare-earth source points store X and Y as Eastings and Northings in OSGB36.
Bare-earth source-point Z values are heights in metres relative to the applicable datum.
Most OS Terrain source areas use Ordnance Datum Newlyn, while a small number of offshore islands use a local datum.
The bare-earth model excludes buildings, supported structures and vegetation.
Ground-level obstructions such as sufficiently large dams, breakwaters, groynes, bridge revetments and earthworks can be treated as part of the bare-earth surface.
Only permanent terrain features expected to remain until the next revision period or longer are modelled.
Underground features are not recorded in the DTM.
Overhead features are removed from the DTM.
Supported structures are removed where they depart from the bare-earth surface and have an air gap.
Vegetation such as hedgerows and trees is removed so the bare-earth surface is recorded.
Major road and rail routes are specifically modelled to reflect their real-world shape.
Road furniture and bridges are removed from major communication-route surfaces during terrain modelling.
Associated slopes and embankments along major communication routes are modelled.
Temporary spoil heaps at mineral or landfill sites are removed when they do not represent the terrain at capture time.
Flat-water bodies greater than 0.7ha have their limits captured so their presence can be inferred from the data.
For those flat-water bodies, the recorded water height is the lowest height of the surrounding data and the water surface is flat.
OS Terrain 50 GML contour data uses ContourLine, SpotHeight and LandWaterBoundary as feature types.
SpotHeight propertyValue stores the feature's z value above Newlyn or another British height datum.
SpotHeight supports formSpot, generic, mountainPass and summit type values, though current features are attributed generic.
LandWaterBoundary supports meanHighWater, meanLowWater, meanHighWaterSprings and meanLowWaterSprings categories.
OS Terrain 50 GML feature IDs use the pattern os.t50.<tile name>.<sequential number>.
Geometry IDs use the same identifier pattern with a .geom suffix.
Features and geometries are guaranteed unique within a given product release.
OS Terrain products are refreshed by whole tile and do not use feature-based change-only updates.
When a tile is updated, sequential feature identifiers are regenerated.
OS Terrain 50 GML expresses British National Grid as urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::27700.
OS Terrain 50 gridded supply includes a .prj file containing the spatial reference system in Esri format.
OS Terrain 50 gridded supply includes an .asc.aux.xml file providing default-style parameters for Esri applications.
Per-tile grid metadata is supplied in a Metadata_<tile name>.xml file containing information such as flying date.
